_note: Continuity ledger for sinusoidal-cycles (Sinusoidal History). Seeded 2026-08-13 during the evening-fleet close-out, when the Phase 12 SEO ship surfaced the first item that needed a machine-trackable close condition rather than a prose note. Before this the project carried state in CHANGELOG.md + agent memory only; those remain the ship log and the narrative record respectively.
bindingConstraint: Discovery — and as of 2026-08-14 we can finally see part of it. The site is a finished, fact-checked artifact with no acquisition path. The 8/14 crawl read (scripts/crawl-read.mjs, over Render's request logs) sharpened the picture: Google has not crawled this site at all in 7 days, while GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot poll it daily and GPTBot has content-crawled the prose pages. So the constraint is not 'nothing can be measured' — it is that the only discovery channel currently working is LLM crawlers, Google is absent entirely, and the human-facing half (impressions, queries, whether a page was ever shown to a person) still needs a Search Console property that does not exist. Retention, sharing, and word-of-mouth remain unmeasurable.
loopArchetype: Reference/explainer — a reader arrives on a specific long-wave theory (via search or a shared link), reads its calibration rationale and paired data, and either opens the interactive chart or leaves. There is no account, no return loop, and no monetisation; the would-tell-a-friend moment is 'this chart made a contested idea legible enough to argue with.'

items.title: sinusoidal-history is measured at last — indexed, 59 impressions, and converting at 0%
items.hypothesis: The 8 per-cycle routes shipped 2026-08-13 target high-intent queries ('Kondratiev wave chart', 'Turchin secular cycle data'). Whether they earn impressions is currently unknowable: there is no verified Google Search Console property for sinusoidal-history.skylarkcreations.com, no PostHog, and no page-view counter anywhere in the app.
items.notes:
Surfaced during the Phase 12 ship (commits 448d974, 6005b92) and deliberately NOT actioned that session — the dispatch's guardrail was 'no analytics decision tonight; note the gap as a follow-up candidate.' So this is a carried thread, not a completed one. Cheapest meaningful close is GSC alone: verifying the property costs one DNS TXT record or an HTML meta tag and immediately answers the impressions question for all 9 new URLs, with no client-side code and no consent/cookie surface added to a site that currently has none. PostHog is the heavier option (portfolio key exists as POSTHOG_API_KEY, project 454749) and would need a privacy note in /colophon, which is a David-voice call rather than an engineering one. Sitemap is already live and lists the index + all 8 routes, so a GSC property can submit it the same day it is verified.

2026-08-14 — PARTIALLY NARROWED, not closed. The premise 'zero analytics' was too strong: Render's own HTTP request logs already record path + user-agent for every hit, so the CRAWL half of this question was answerable all along with no instrumentation, no client script, and no consent surface. Built `scripts/crawl-read.mjs` (reads the Render logs API, aggregates by crawler; `--selfcheck` covers the UA-classification and label-parsing logic) and ran a 7-day read. Findings: (1) ZERO Google hits of any kind in 7 days — not Googlebot, not Google-Extended. Google does not appear to know this site exists, which means the bottleneck is discovery-by-Google, and no amount of additional SEO surface fixes that; the GSC property is the unblock and it is now evidence-backed rather than speculative. (2) There IS a live discovery channel already working: GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot poll /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml on a DAILY cadence (~15:2x UTC, unbroken 8/07-8/13), and GPTBot ran a full content crawl on 2026-08-12 17:43 covering /, /about, /methods, /colophon, /poster, /embed/docs. This is the first real evidence this project has ever had about who wants it, and it vindicates the llms.txt + .md-mirror strategy. (3) That GPTBot content crawl PREDATES the Phase 12 ship by a day, so it saw none of the 8 new routes; GPTBot has since re-fetched the sitemap (8/13 15:32Z) which now lists them. No crawler has fetched a /cycles* page yet. What crawl logs still CANNOT answer: impressions, queries, ranking position, or whether an indexed page was ever shown to a human. Those still need GSC, so the close condition below is unchanged.

2026-08-15 — THE PHASE 12 ROUTES ARE BEING CRAWLED. Read 6 days early because the 8/15 P2 continuity pass ran the instrument rather than waiting for the 08-21 date; the gate was already readable. `node scripts/crawl-read.mjs --days 7` at 2026-08-15T15:2xZ: GPTBot ran a full content crawl at 2026-08-15T10:27:04Z-10:27:38Z covering / , /cycles, ALL EIGHT /cycles/<slug> routes (kondratiev, schlesinger-jr, strauss-howe, perez, dalio, turchin, khaldun, huntington) AND all eight ?focus=<id> deep links, then returned at 10:54Z for RSC navigation payloads (/?_rsc=...&focus=perez, /cycles?_rsc=...) — i.e. it was traversing the app's client routing, not just fetching static URLs. This ANSWERS question (a) of the old 08-21 read with a YES and closes it. Derived latency, useful for future ships: the sitemap first listed the 8 routes on 2026-08-13 15:32Z (GPTBot's own re-fetch) and the content crawl landed 2026-08-15 10:27Z — approximately 43 hours, across two intervening daily sitemap polls (8/14 15:37Z, 8/15 10:27Z). So a new route on this site is LLM-crawled in about two days, and the internal-linking worry in the old branching was unfounded — no action needed there. This is the first evidence this project has ever had that a discovery channel is actually delivering to its newest surface.

Still open and UNCHANGED: Google is at ZERO for the 7-day window — no Googlebot, no Google-Extended, no Google-other. Positive control for that zero (per the number-provenance floor): the same classifier recorded 67 GPTBot + 9 OAI-SearchBot + 1 other-bot hits in the same window, the classified buckets sum exactly to the 2401 raw log lines, and `--selfcheck` unit-asserts the Googlebot and Google-Extended branches specifically — so a Google hit would have been recorded had one occurred. The zero is measured, not a dead probe.

CAUTION on the non-crawler buckets — do NOT report these as humans. The same read shows 1481 'browser-ish' and 778 'unknown (no UA)' lines (~323/day). 'browser-ish' is a UA-SHAPE fallback bucket (anything that is not a known crawler, not empty, and not our own tooling), and the number-provenance floor requires that crawler/human attribution verify official IP ranges rather than UA strings alone. On a site with zero Google presence and no inbound links, ~323/day of browser-shaped traffic is far more likely to be scanners and scrapers with spoofed UAs than readers. Treat the human-residual question as OPEN and unanswered; answering it needs reverse-DNS / IP-range verification, which is a bigger change than reporting the existing bucket.

2026-08-18 — RE-SEQUENCED by the citability research + domain purchase. (1) The two-engine citability research (skylark-site research-library 2026-08-18-sinusoidal-cycles-citability.md) confirmed GSC verification as the #1 evidence-backed config action — Google indexing is a categorical prerequisite for AI Overviews — and simultaneously RETIRED GPTBot crawl depth as a KPI (training-only traffic, ~1,700 crawls per referral; the new proxy hierarchy is utm_source=chatgpt.com referrals > ChatGPT-User > OAI-SearchBot). (2) David bought sinusoidalhistory.com AND .org on 2026-08-18 (renew Aug 2027). The GSC property should therefore be created on the NEW domain AFTER the cutover, not on the skylarkcreations.com subdomain — verifying the old host first would mean verifying twice. Order: domain cutover (301s from old subdomain preserve the proven GPTBot channel) → GSC on sinusoidalhistory.com → sitemap submit. The 08-21 crawl re-read below still stands as written.

2026-08-20 — THE UNBLOCK LANDED. Domain cutover shipped (commit d36770b): sinusoidalhistory.com is canonical; the legacy subdomain, the .org twin, and both www variants issue permanent redirects with paths preserved (verified live end-to-end, including /cycles/turchin and the frozen /data/state-2026.csv). David added the DNS records, verified a Google Search Console property on the NEW domain (hello@skylarkcreations.com), and SUBMITTED sitemap.xml — so the W-001 sequencing (cutover → GSC → sitemap) is complete on all three legs. robots.txt on the new domain also declares the sitemap, so discovery does not depend on the manual submit. What remains is purely a WAIT: Google needs time to crawl a domain it has never seen. TWO reads, deliberately staged. (a) SOON — 2026-08-22: did the PROVEN channel survive the host change? GPTBot/OAI-SearchBot polled robots.txt + sitemap.xml daily on the old subdomain; the question is whether they follow the 308 onto sinusoidalhistory.com and resume the daily cadence there. If that goes silent, the cutover broke the one discovery channel that was actually working and it is urgent, not a wait. (b) LATER — 2026-09-03: the Google question. GSC was verified 2026-08-20, so a zero before a fresh 14-day window from that date means nothing; do not read it as the cutover failing.

2026-08-21 — BOTH STAGED QUESTIONS ANSWERED EARLY, AND THE BIG ONE FLIPPED: GOOGLE ARRIVED. Ran the 14-day read one day ahead of the 8/22 date because two post-cutover daily-poll windows had already passed (same early-read precedent as 8/15). Findings, in severity order. (1) The 'Google at zero' era is OVER: 731 Google-family hits in the window (188 Googlebot + 543 Google-other), ALL post-cutover — Googlebot fetched sitemap.xml 2026-08-20 22:18Z, hours after David submitted it through the new GSC property, then polled robots.txt near-hourly overnight and content-crawled /cycles/<slug> routes, /data/spectral/*.svg, and the paired CSVs through 8/21 17:08Z. Google-other (likely GoogleOther/InspectionTool onboarding the new domain) swept every page including all 10 cycle routes, /llms.txt, and /about.md. (2) Read (a) answered YES: the LLM channel survived the host change — OAI-SearchBot observed following the old-host 308 to a 200 on the new host in the same second (8 hits in the trailing 24h), and GPTBot crawled in-window: 13 sitemap fetches, all 10 cycle routes, all spectral SVGs + verdicts.json, the v1 API, and the frozen state-2026.csv (200 hits/14d; 2 in the trailing 24h). The channel-break escalation branch is dead. (3) Provenance: complete=true, buckets sum (11,883 lines), snapshot appended to docs/crawl-reads.jsonl. Instrument note: Render's API allows 30 req/min and the 14-day read paginates ~119 pages, so crawl-read.mjs now backs off on 429 instead of dying — three consecutive runs had failed before the fix; selfcheck still passes. NEXT: the 2026-09-03 read is now the GSC INDEXING question (coverage + first impressions/queries per onTrigger), not 'is Google present' — that is answered.

2026-09-08 — THE CRAWL LEG OF THE 09-03 GATE IS ANSWERED (5 days late; the project had no session between 08-30 and 09-08, so the gate simply went unread — nothing blocked it). This was also the FIRST time this row's readCommand ever executed through the gate: the first attempt was killed at the 60s default cap, because a 14-day read paginates ~250 pages against Render's 30 req/min logs API and crawl-read.mjs backs off on 429 by design, so the backoff waits ARE the runtime. Raised readCommandTimeoutMs to the 600000ms cap; the re-run took 548s, exit 0, complete=true, 25,215 log lines, snapshot #3 appended to docs/crawl-reads.jsonl. Findings, in severity order. (1) GOOGLE HELD AND DEEPENED. Googlebot 375 hits/14d (was 188 in the 08-21 window — roughly doubled) and it is now CONTENT-crawling, not onboarding: 9 of the 10 /cycles/<slug> routes (all but modelski), all 8 paired data CSVs at 5 fetches each, the .md prose mirrors (about.md, methods.md, colophon.md), llms.txt, and the spectral SVGs. Google-family TOTAL fell 731 -> 447 only because the one-off GoogleOther onboarding sweep (543 -> 48) is over; the sustained-crawl number is the one that doubled. The llms.txt + .md-mirror + reuse-packet strategy is being consumed by Googlebot, not just LLM crawlers. (2) BING ARRIVED, UNPROMPTED AND AT PARITY. Bingbot 373 hits/14d, absent entirely from the 08-21 read. It crawled ALL 10 cycle routes plus /cycles (20), /methods (19), /poster (18), /about (18), /embed/docs (20), /state/2026 (13). No Bing Webmaster Tools property exists — this is organic discovery off robots.txt/sitemap. A second search engine is now a live channel and is UNMEASURED on the impressions side, exactly as Google was before 08-20. (3) THE LLM CHANNEL BROADENED — BUT THE PER-CRAWLER TOTALS ARE PARTLY SPOOFED, SO READ COVERAGE, NOT byWho. A single vulnerability scan on 2026-08-28 08:28-08:31Z made 643 requests while ROTATING crawler user-agents, and the classifier attributed them by UA: 68 'Meta/Facebook', 57 'OAI-SearchBot', 55 'GPTBot', 51 'Amazonbot', 27 'Applebot', 26 'PerplexityBot', 23 'Bytespider', 20 'Google-Extended', 19 'ClaudeBot', 295 'other bot'. That is 83% of Google-Extended's entire 14-day total, 62% of Bytespider's, 60% of Meta's, ~35% of Amazonbot/Applebot/PerplexityBot. Whatever claimed to be GPTBot while requesting /api-keys.json was not GPTBot. This does NOT touch the findings above: the snapshot's per-crawler COVERAGE map is keyed on real site paths and excludes the 404 probe paths, so route-level claims are sound while the byWho volume column is not. Judged by coverage, the genuinely content-crawling set is: Googlebot, Bingbot, OAI-SearchBot (every cycle route + every .source.md + all three /api/v1 endpoints), GPTBot, Amazonbot (40 distinct paths incl. all 10 cycle routes) and Applebot. Real but shallow: PerplexityBot (6 paths), Meta/Facebook (6 — but notably /llms.txt + all three .md mirrors), ClaudeBot (3). Effectively absent from content: Bytespider (/robots.txt only) and Google-Extended (ZERO real paths — its 24 hits are the spoof burst plus robots noise, which is why its coverage map is empty). So 'eight crawlers' is the wrong headline; SIX crawl the content and two of the eight are noise. (4) THE HUMAN-RESIDUAL QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED IN THE NEGATIVE, and the 08-15 CAUTION should be read as confirmed rather than open: the snapshot's own path list shows the 18,572 'browser-ish' + 3,395 'unknown (no UA)' lines are dominated by vulnerability scanning — /.env and ~40 variants of it, /wp-config.php, /secrets.json, /terraform.tfstate, /root/.aws/credentials, /serviceAccountKey.json. Do NOT report those buckets as readers. (Not an incident: static Next.js, none of those paths exist; this is internet background noise.) STILL OPEN and now the ONLY open leg: impressions, queries, ranking position, and index coverage — the human-facing half. That needs the GSC console read on David's account and cannot be derived from request logs at all. Bing Webmaster Tools is now a second, cheap instrument worth the same one-time verification David did for GSC on 08-20.

2026-09-09 — THE LAST OPEN LEG IS ANSWERED, AND W-001 NARROWS TO A CTR WATCH RATHER THAN CLOSING. David returned the Search Console read (card ef5842ec, answered 2026-09-09T20:24Z); the numbers here are the orchestrator read of David's screenshots, card ef5842ec, not an agent-run instrument. Property sinusoidalhistory.com, Search type Web, last 3 months, data current to ~9.5h before 14:23 MT: Total clicks 0, Total impressions 59, Average CTR 0%, Average position 16. Pages tab lists 14 pages; top 10 by impressions: /methods 13, /cycles/perez 9, /cycles 8, /cycles/schlesinger-jr 7, /cycles/turchin-fathers-sons 6, /cycles/huntington 5, /cycles/strauss-howe 5, /about 4, / 4, /colophon 2 — every one at 0 clicks. Impressions begin ~8/21 on the daily chart, matching the 08-20 sitemap submit. DISPOSITION: the onTrigger branch that fired is 'indexed with impressions', so this converts to a measurement watch exactly as pre-registered — but that branch's named payoff, the first non-brand query set, is NOT collectable: the Queries tab reads 'No data' because GSC suppresses query rows below an anonymity/volume threshold and 59 impressions sits under it. So the row NARROWS rather than closing. Indexing is proven (14 pages shown), which kills the 'crawled but excluded from the index' diagnosis branch before its 09-19 threshold. The open question is no longer 'are we visible' but 'why does visibility convert at 0%'. At position ~16 the only user-visible surface is the SERP snippet — the title tag and the meta description — and this session shipped a rewrite of exactly that surface (see linkedCommits). What it found there, none of it visible from inside the app, which is why it survived four fact-check rounds and a journey walk: SIX pages emitted the site name twice in the title ('Methods · Sinusoidal History · Sinusoidal History', live-verified on /methods, /about, /colophon, /poster, /embed/docs and /embed); the home page's own description undercounted the site's content as 'Eight historical cycle theories' while cycles.json held ten; and every per-cycle description spent its first ~45 characters repeating the cycle name already in the title, leaked a chart-legend qualifier ('Paired with Tech diffusion · site-derived'), and overran Google's ~155-character fold at 195. The next read is therefore a CTR read, not a coverage read.

2026-09-16 — THE READ MOVED FROM DAVID'S SCREEN TO AN AGENT COMMAND. skylark-site ae4e4460f wires 'sinusoidal-cycles' -> 'sc-domain:sinusoidalhistory.com' into GSC_PROPERTIES; the property reads siteOwner and the auth chain validated. First programmatic read ran today from this lane against the same client /api/cc/gsc-performance wraps. (The ROUTE 400s until Render deploys ae4e4460f — deployed sha at read time was 2e56643f. The CLI reads the local registry and does not wait, which is why the readCommand below is the CLI and not the route.)

WINDOW + n. Search Console holds data 2026-08-19 -> 2026-09-13; there is a ~3-day reporting lag, so no same-day read can ever see the last 2-3 days. PRE 1136b87 (2026-08-19..2026-09-09): 73 impressions, 0 clicks, avg position 16.4. POST (2026-09-10..2026-09-13 — 4 days with data): 16 impressions, 0 clicks, avg position 21.4. David's 59-impression figure is a shorter UI window over this same series, not a different measurement.

DID 1136b87 MOVE CLICK-THROUGH OFF ZERO? Unanswerable at this n — a question, not a verdict. 16 post-ship impressions at average position ~21 predicts well under one click even at a healthy CTR, so this zero carries no information in either direction. The instrument now exists; the sample does not. Do not re-read before ~2026-10-07 expecting an answer.

THE PAYOFF THIS ROW HAS CARRIED SINCE 2026-08-13 IS IN — the first non-brand query set. 5 query rows surface (GSC's privacy threshold anonymizes the rest, so 5 of 89 impressions carry a visible query), and 4 of the 5 are Ray Dalio: "ray dalio big cycle" (2 impr, pos 60.0), "ray dalio big cycle theory" (1, pos 49.0), "ray dalio the big cycle" (1, pos 55.0), "ray dalio big cycles" (1, pos 52.0). The fifth is "cycle of ten" (1, pos 8.0). Every Dalio query sits at position 49-60 — page 5 or 6, where CTR is ~0 whatever the snippet says. The demand that exists is for a NAMED THEORY, and the site is nowhere near the first page for it.

PAGE SPLIT MOVED, AND IT IS NOISE SO FAR. Pre-ship, /methods was the top page (14 of 73 impressions, pos 11.3). Post-ship, /methods drew 0 impressions in 4 days while /cycles/dalio drew 8 of 16 at pos 33.9. Do NOT read that as the rewrite demoting /methods: n=16 over 4 days, and the Dalio share matches the surfaced queries.

INSTRUMENT CHANGE (orchestrator-approved 2026-09-16, bus msg 2655180f). Organic clicks by page is this lane's tier-1 read; scripts/crawl-read.mjs drops to a MONTHLY coverage check. readCommand is now the portfolio demand worklist, which prints the non-brand-clicks baseline (the ONE metric) plus the demand-gap queries. Its own caveat: brand classification is regex-advisory, and "sinusoidal history" is the only brand string here — every query above is non-brand.

2026-09-16 (P2) — READ COMMAND CORRECTED TO PAGE-ONLY GROUPING. The worklist set earlier today derives its clicks from QUERY-grouped rows, and Search Console drops anonymized-query rows from any query grouping, so its click count undercounts (orchestrator catch, bus df65abc0). readCommand is now scripts/gsc-read.mjs, which reads /api/cc/gsc-performance grouped by page only — the one grouping whose totals are whole. The worklist stays the right tool for the QUERY LIST only. Verified the same day: the route (deployed; skylark-site ae4e4460f is an ancestor of the live sha) returns PRE 2026-08-19..09-09 = 73 impressions / 0 clicks / position 16.4 — identical to the direct client read above — and POST 2026-09-10..09-16 = 17 / 0 / 20.4 (one more day of data than this morning). Post-ship /methods: 1 impression at position 5.0.

DATE LABEL. 1136b87 was committed 2026-09-09 20:39 MT (19:39 Pacific). Search Console days are Pacific, so the 09-09 bucket is mixed (pre-ship until 19:39) and is counted as PRE. The 09-19 read is ten MT days after the ship.

CLOSEWHEN, FIRST CLAUSE NOW MET: a property is verified for the canonical domain and impressions/clicks are observable. The second clause (sitemap submitted through that property) is unverified. Not converted — ruling left to the orchestrator.



2026-09-19 (P2) — READ RUN, AND THE DATE MOVES TO 2026-10-07 UNDER THIS ROW'S OWN BRANCH 0. `node scripts/gsc-read.mjs --start 2026-09-10` at 2026-09-19T15:09Z: window 2026-09-10..2026-09-19, sc-domain:sinusoidalhistory.com, TOTAL clicks=0 impressions=19 position=21.0. Per page: /cycles/dalio 9 impressions at position 35.7; /about, /cycles/kondratiev and /state/2026 at 2 each (positions 6.0, 5.0, 10.0); / , /cycles/khaldun, /cycles/perez, /cycles/schlesinger-jr, /cycles/turchin-fathers-sons and /methods at 1 each. The page list truncates at the route's row limit; the TOTAL line is whole. DISPOSITION — BRANCH 0 HOLDS: 19 post-ship impressions is far under N_min=100, so every discriminator in the branching is INAPPLICABLE and this read is a sample-size check, not a verdict. Taking disposition (a) as written: extend to 2026-10-07, the row's own stated first answerable date (~30 days post-ship), and re-read then. Explicitly NOT (b) escalate — the instrument is proven, the same read returns nonzero impressions through the same pipeline — and NOT (c) accept directionally-clear-but-thin, because a zero-click column has no direction. WHICH LEVER MOVED: neither, and at this n neither could. Position 21.0 against the 2026-09-16 POST baseline of 20.4 is a 0.6 drift on n=19; /cycles/dalio holding 9 of 19 impressions continues the Dalio-dominated share the 09-16 query read already explained (every Dalio query sat at position 49-60). The totals are byte-identical to this lane's 09-17 and 09-18 reads (19/0/21.0) — those two are witnessed by this lane's session records only, not by a stamped artifact, so treat the three-read identity as this row's own account rather than a cited measurement. The cause is Search Console's ~3-day reporting lag: no new day had entered the window, which is why a daily re-read of this instrument returns the same bytes. Extension approved by the orchestrator at 2026-09-19T15:21Z (bus msgId 48554209-4891-49de-a2ea-24ab6ea97cb8); the row's Branch 0 already prescribed it.



2026-09-19 (P4, waits gate) — THE 2026-10-07 DATE SITS AT THE OPTIMISTIC EDGE OF N_min, AND THIS IS THE PRE-REGISTERED ANSWER SO THE ROW IS NOT RE-DATED A SECOND TIME. Measured rate, from today's read rather than assumed: 19 post-ship impressions over the 7 days Search Console actually holds data for (2026-09-10..~09-16, at its ~3-day reporting lag) = ~2.7/day. The 09-16 note assumed ~4/day; that figure is now superseded by measurement. Projected to the 2026-10-07 read, whose data will cover through ~10-04 (~25 days post-ship): ~68 impressions at the measured rate, ~100 at the old assumed rate. So N_min=100 is reachable only at the optimistic end, and the honest expectation is a read that is still under the floor. DISPOSITION IF 10-07 LANDS SHORT, fixed here in advance: do NOT extend the date again. The waits gate (2026-07-18, section 7.150) forbids re-dating a data-wait whose denominator does not fill by its own read date, and a second extension would be exactly that. Convert instead to the read that IS answerable at that n, which this row's own nextTrigger already names: did the query set grow beyond the five Dalio-dominated rows, and did average position move off ~21. CTR then stops being this row's question. It reopens as a fresh row only if average position moves under 20, which is the point at which a zero-click column starts carrying information.

2026-09-20 (P4, waits gate) — THE CTR QUESTION IS RETIRED TODAY RATHER THAN ON 10-07, AND THE DATE DOES NOT MOVE. The gate asks whether a data-wait's denominator can FILL by its own read date. Yesterday's measurement says it cannot: ~2.7 impressions/day projects to ~68 by the 10-07 read against N_min=100. The gate's remedy for that is re-point, convert or retire — never re-date. Yesterday PRE-REGISTERED the conversion for the day itself; today it is APPLIED, because a wait already known to land short is not a wait, it is a scheduled disappointment, and holding it for another 17 days would have bought nothing but the disappointment. So CTR stops being this row's question as of today. The 2026-10-07 read is RE-POINTED to the two questions that are answerable at n≈68 — did the query set grow beyond the five Dalio-dominated rows, and did average position move off ~21 — and the date itself is UNCHANGED at 2026-10-07. Click-through reopens as a FRESH row only if average position moves under 20. FREEZE VALIDITY, checked in the same pass: the freeze on titles, meta descriptions, H1s and URLs still protects a READABLE read, because both converted questions are snippet- and rank-sensitive and their denominator is filling at a measured rate; it HOLDS, with the same 2026-10-07 expiry, and lifts with the read rather than outliving it.
items.closeWhen: A Google Search Console property is verified for the site's canonical domain (sinusoidalhistory.com after the cutover; the old subdomain only if the cutover is abandoned) AND /sitemap.xml has been submitted through it — at which point impressions/clicks become observable and this converts to a measurement watch. Alternatively closes as 'declined' if David decides the site should stay uninstrumented.
items.onTrigger: AS OF 2026-09-20 THIS ROW'S QUESTION IS NO LONGER CTR — see the P4 waits-gate entry in notes. The 2026-10-07 read asks the two things answerable at n≈68: did the query set grow beyond the five Dalio-dominated rows, and did average position move off ~21. Report clicks anyway, but do not read a zero as a verdict; click-through reopens as a fresh row only if average position moves under 20. The rest of this field is the pre-conversion instruction, kept because its cautions still bind. Coverage and the first non-brand query set were both answered on 2026-09-16 and are recorded in this row's notes — do NOT re-ask for them. What remains is CTR over time, read with this row's readCommand (scripts/gsc-read.mjs, page-only grouping so click totals are whole). On each read: report the window and n, compare clicks / impressions / average position PER PAGE against the 2026-09-16 baseline (PRE 73 impressions / 0 clicks / position 16.4; POST 17 / 0 / 20.4), and say which lever moved — snippet (CTR at a held position) or rank (position itself). If any of the 11 indexed URLs drops out of the page list for 30+ days, diagnose indexing (canonical conflict, thin content, crawl budget) before writing more SEO surface. Standing caution: the query rows are a SAMPLE — Search Console anonymizes low-volume queries, so 5 rows sat under 89 impressions on the first read; never read the query list as the whole demand, and never take a click total from a query-grouped read.

items.title: Next.js 16.2.4 -> 16.3.5: the only bump that closes the 30 remaining Dependabot alerts
items.notes:
Dependabot alerts were switched on for this public repo on 2026-09-16 after the close (bus 75b79c2e) and reported 46 open — new coverage, not new breakage. 2026-09-17: a400821 applied every same-range fix (npm audit fix without --force, plus vitest and @vitest/ui to ^4.1.11, both dev-only) and the alert list itself went 46 -> 30, read twice with `gh api repos/u00dxk2/sinusoidal-history/dependabot/alerts?state=open --paginate` (16:05Z before, 17:05Z after). CI green on Linux for that commit; a before/after snapshot of the visible text of all 20 prerendered pages plus the emitted CSS showed 0 differences on identical source, red-armed by mutating a page hash and a CSS hash (the diff names both and exits 3).

The 30 that remain are one bump: 24 on `next` itself, 4 on the `postcss` copy nested inside `next`, 2 on `sharp` which `next` pulls in. npm only fixes them with `npm audit fix --force`, which installs next@16.3.5 — outside the exact 16.2.4 this repo pins. Two of the 24 are rated critical, and neither describes this deployment as verified today: one is remote code execution on Windows-hosted servers (this deploys to Render on Linux), the other is remote code execution in the Image Optimization API via AVIF. The site renders no next/image component, but /_next/image answers 200 in production; next.config.ts declares no images.remotePatterns, so that endpoint reads same-origin paths only and the site accepts no uploads. The twelve middleware/proxy-bypass advisories describe a middleware.ts this repo does not have (glob over `middleware.{ts,js}` and `src/middleware.{ts,js}`: no files).

Held rather than shipped because AGENTS.md's first line is that this Next differs from what a model remembers, and its JSX whitespace hazard is compiler behaviour — a framework bump can change rendered prose that is correct today. The gate that answers it already exists and is the one used above.
items.closeWhen: MET the same day. The orchestrator ruled under default-decision authority (bus 15ac3b4b, 2026-09-17T17:02Z) and dismissed the board card; the bump shipped in 7dadae1 and the alert list reads 0 open.
items.resolution: SHIPPED 2026-09-17. next and eslint-config-next 16.2.4 -> 16.3.5, both pins still exact. The gate was held: all 20 prerendered pages' visible text identical, and the emitted CSS identical once per-build font-asset URL tokens are normalized — the RAW CSS did differ, in 14 @font-face url() cache-buster suffixes only (same 743 rules, same 60,063 bytes, font content hashes unchanged), so the first reading was dirty and the second clean. CI GREEN on Linux for 7dadae1, live 17:37:52Z, frame read at 390 and 1440 on production clean. `gh api repos/u00dxk2/sinusoidal-history/dependabot/alerts?state=open --paginate` -> 0 open at 17:44Z, from 46 this morning. The engineeringZeroWaiver is REMOVED rather than re-dated, because its reason no longer exists — a waiver outliving its reason is how a panel goes quietly green. Also answered as a condition of the ruling: the AGENTS.md JSX whitespace hazard did not reproduce on 16.3.5 in the two cases probed, recorded there version-scoped.

items.title: The roster slug sinusoidal-cycles resolves to no workspace entry, so five kickoff state reads and agent-status's verify-receipt gate silently do not run on this lane
items.hypothesis: resolve-project-path looks up the roster slug 'sinusoidal-cycles' in skylark-site's src/data/cc-workspace.json, which holds this lane under the id 'sinusoidal'. The lookup is by id, so the roster slug matches nothing and every caller that resolves a lane by slug returns NO_LANE_ROOT. Nothing about the checkout, the path, or this repo is wrong.
items.notes:
OPENED 2026-09-20 at P2 on the orchestrator's instruction (bus 398c7062), after being carried unrowed for three days: named in this lane's P1 on 2026-09-18, carried on 2026-09-19 to 'skylark-site/2026-09-19/the resolver-fallback ship' — which names a date, not an id, so it rendered CARRIED-UNROWED and was findable from neither side. That is the entire reason this row exists; the fix itself is relayed to the orchestrator and is NOT this lane's to make.

THE FIX, CORRECTED. Add 'sinusoidal-cycles' as an id ALIAS onto the EXISTING 'sinusoidal' entry in skylark-site src/data/cc-workspace.json. No path change and no new entry: read at cc-workspace.json:121-123, that entry already carries path 'C:/dev/skylark/sinusoidal-cycles', which is this checkout. An earlier version of this diagnosis (this lane's P1 today, bus 8b193502) said the path pointed at 'C:/dev/skylark/sinusoidal-history' and that a junction was involved; the orchestrator read the file at skylark-site HEAD and corrected it, and I confirmed the corrected reading myself with a grep of that file. Carry the corrected version. LOOSE END, stated as a hypothesis and not a finding: the string 'sinusoidal-history' does appear in the dispatch pre-flight header of today's kickoff ('sinusoidal-cycles @ C:/dev/skylark/sinusoidal-history'), and C:/dev/skylark/sinusoidal-history does exist on this machine and resolves to this same worktree (git -C ... rev-parse --show-toplevel returns C:/dev/skylark/sinusoidal-cycles). It is also the repo's GitHub name (u00dxk2/sinusoidal-history). Whoever makes the edit should know that pre-flight leg gets its path from somewhere other than the cc-workspace entry; I have not traced which, and it is not part of the fix.

MEASURED IMPACT, 2026-09-20. In ONE kickoff body, five state reads returned UNREADABLE naming this cause — dated gates, primer, primer banner, listener, HEAD CI — while the same body's dispatch pre-flight leg resolved this lane successfully and read real values off this tree (vitest ^4.1.11, ci.yml:18, eslint reach). Three agent-status posts today (8b193502, d8fe7bfa, 1cf79fad) each printed 'verify-receipt: UNREADABLE for lane sinusoidal-cycles ... The gate did NOT run'. read-listener-strand.mjs exits 2 NO_LANE_ROOT. Yesterday the same gate was skipped on all five of that session's posts.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE NOISE SUGGESTS. From the composer's side a clean listener strand and total deafness on this lane read identically, because neither can be measured — so no arrival surface can tell this pane it has been missing work. The UNREADABLE lines themselves are cheap to skip past; what is not cheap is that a whole class of question about this lane is currently unanswerable and looks merely verbose.
items.closeWhen: skylark-site's src/data/cc-workspace.json resolves the slug 'sinusoidal-cycles' to this checkout, evidenced by this row's readCommand exiting 0 with a listener strand instead of exit 2 NO_LANE_ROOT, AND an agent-status post from this lane printing a verify-receipt verdict rather than UNREADABLE. Closes as 'declined' if the orchestrator rules that the roster slug should change to 'sinusoidal' instead — that is an equally valid fix and would close this row just as well.
items.onTrigger: Run the readCommand. Exit 0 with strand lines = fixed; close the row, link the skylark-site commit, and say in the same post whether a verify-receipt verdict now prints on a real post, because the strand read and the gate are two different callers and one can be fixed without the other. Exit 2 NO_LANE_ROOT = not fixed; do NOT re-derive the diagnosis (it is complete in notes) and do NOT edit cc-workspace.json from this lane — it is written by /api/cc/save-config and is skylark-site's file. Re-raise it in one line on the bus against this row id and re-date once. If it is still open on the second re-date, that is a signal the relay is not reaching the owner, which is a different problem than the bug and should be said that way.

The fix lives in another repo and was relayed to the orchestrator the same day, so a daily re-read would only re-measure someone else's queue; a week is long enough for the edit to land through a normal fleet cycle and short enough that a fourth silent day cannot become a fourth silent week. The date is deliberately at the TOP LEVEL of this item, per meta.signalDateField and the note there — a nested date resolves to undefined and the row would read as date-less to every overdue scanner while the dashboard showed green.

items.title: Does a phone reader understand a cycle's confidence tag at first contact, now that the written glossary follows the roster instead of preceding it?
items.hypothesis: Probably yes, and the cost is smaller than it first looked — but the part that is genuinely unanswered is touch. A reader on a phone gets no hover, meets NARRATIVE or EMPIRICAL · CONTESTED beside the first entry, and the written definition is now below ten entries and a table.
items.notes:
OPENED 2026-09-20 at P4, to discharge a promise I had left with no reader and no date. The 2026-09-20 P3 ship (2d693ac) re-ordered /cycles so the ten entries clear the phone fold, which moved the confidence-tag glossary BELOW the roster. I declared that cost in the P3 post and wrote the resolution condition as 'if a cold walk reports the tags reading as unexplained' — the orchestrator correctly called that a promise with no reader and no date, which is the exact shape I refuse to accept from an instrument. Hence this row.

WHAT THE COST ACTUALLY IS, measured rather than assumed. The tag is NOT undefined: src/app/(app)/cycles/[id]/page.tsx:247-253 renders 'Confidence classification: <LABEL> — <gloss>.' on EVERY per-cycle page, and each index entry links to exactly that page. So the definition is one click away from the tag on the destination the entry already points at, and it is also still on the index itself, below. Journey-walk 2026-08-24 J8's finding was that the tags 'were defined nowhere on the site'; that is no longer the accurate description of this regression. What changed is ORDER on one page, not existence.

WHAT SHIPPED WITH THIS ROW. The index tag now carries title={confidenceGloss(...)} — the gloss on hover and keyboard focus. It is an ATTRIBUTE, so it adds no visible text and costs no vertical space, which is the whole reason it was chosen: a visible pointer line above the entries would push the second entry's name back below the 390x664 fold and undo the ship it is meant to soften. It does nothing on touch. That is the honest limit and it is why this row exists rather than the work being declared done.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. Making the tag itself a link to #confidence-tags would work on touch, but the tag sits inside the entry's block <Link> and nesting an anchor inside an anchor is invalid HTML; the fix requires splitting the entry's click target, which is a real change to an affordance that journey-walk J11 deliberately introduced. Not worth doing blind — do it if the read below says the tag is not landing, not before.
items.closeWhen: A cold read of /cycles at 390x664 on the question 'what do you think NARRATIVE means here, and where would you look' either (a) reports the tag reads as understood or ignorable, in which case this closes as no-action, or (b) reports it reads as unexplained, in which case the fix is an affordance pointing at #confidence-tags — split the entry's click target so the tag can be an anchor — and this closes when that ships. Closes as 'declined' if the /cycles glossary ever returns above the roster, since the question stops existing.
items.onTrigger: Capture the frame with this row's readCommand and read it COLD — as someone who has not seen this page, looking at the first entry's metadata line. The question is narrow: does NARRATIVE beside '30Y · PEAK 1970' read as a classification whose meaning is findable, or as jargon? Do NOT answer it from the desktop hover state, which is not what a phone reader gets. If the verdict is (b), the fix is named in closeWhen and the frame is the evidence. Either way record the verdict in notes with the date — a read nobody wrote down is this row's own failure mode.
items._nextEvaluationNote: Set 2026-09-20 at row creation, one week out — the same clock as I-001 so this lane carries one gate date rather than two. One week is long enough that the page is settled and short enough that an undiscovered comprehension defect does not sit through a whole GSC window. The date is TOP-LEVEL per meta.signalDateField; a nested date resolves to undefined and the row would read as date-less to every overdue scanner.
items._readCommandNote: This command produces the ARTIFACT the read is made against; it does not itself return a verdict, and it cannot — comprehension is a judgment, not an exit code. Stated plainly so nobody reads a green exit here as the question being answered. The frame is viewport-clipped at 390x664 on purpose: a full-page screenshot cannot show what a reader meets first, which is the whole subject of this row.
items.waitingFor: Nothing and nobody. This is a dated self-read, not a wait on David, the orchestrator or another lane.

knownPatterns.title: Prose that asserts where a cycle sits in a given year drifts from the math
knownPatterns.detail: Round 4 of the external fact-check found the Strauss-Howe rationale claiming '2020 is a trough' when cos(2p*65/84) is approximately +0.15 (rising arm); an internal sweep found the same class of error in Turchin's parenthetical. Both survived three earlier fact-check rounds because nobody did the arithmetic. Phase 12 responded structurally: the per-cycle pages DERIVE their peak/trough years from reference_peak_year + period_years via the same cosine the chart draws (peakYearsInRange / troughYearsInRange in src/lib/cycleRoutes.ts, unit-tested against sineAtYear), so that class of claim can no longer be authored by hand. Any NEW year-phase prose still has to clear `python scripts/audit_cycle_rationales.py` per AGENTS.md.

knownPatterns.title: This Next version's JSX compiler eats element-adjacent spaces in multi-line text nodes
knownPatterns.detail: Live-verified 2026-08-24: a JSX text node that spans multiple source lines loses its leading/trailing whitespace even when the space sits on the same line as an adjacent inline element or {expression} — 'the {year} reading' rendered as 'the 2026reading', 'estimation conventionally' as 'estimationconventionally', symmetric case included ('theamplitude_normalized'). Single-line text nodes are unaffected, which is why the bug is invisible in source review and survives lint/tsc. A 31-junction sweep (9 files, commit e0b8422) converted every affected space to an explicit {" "}; the writing rule is recorded in AGENTS.md. Verify new prose against RENDERED HTML, not the TSX.

knownPatterns.title: A Next.js bump changes the emitted CSS bytes without changing a single style
knownPatterns.detail: Measured on the 16.2.4 -> 16.3.5 bump (2026-09-17, commit 7dadae1). A rendered-output gate that hashes the emitted CSS file reads DIRTY across a Next version change even when nothing visual moves: the 14 @font-face rules carry `url(../media/<contenthash>-s[.p].<token>.woff2)`, and that trailing <token> is a per-BUILD identifier that the bundler regenerates. Everything that matters was identical — 743 rules both sides, 60,063 bytes both sides, and the <contenthash> prefix (the font's own bytes) unchanged. Normalize that token away before comparing, and mind the shape: three of the live tokens contained a dot (`0zgw-jeven.3w`), so a pattern using [^.)]+ for the token silently fails to match on one side and manufactures a difference. Independent confirmation that a normalized-clean read is a real clean read: the production frames re-captured after the deploy were BYTE-IDENTICAL to the ones committed before it. Do not read this class of diff as a reason to revert; do not skip the CSS leg either, because a real restyle looks nothing like this. 2026-09-18: the TEXT leg of that gate is now committed as scripts/check-rendered-text.mjs (e5c53c4) — snap before, diff after, over a URL, an .html file, a directory of them, or a saved snapshot. The CSS leg is deliberately NOT in it, for the reason this row exists; rebuild that part per the normalization above when a bump needs it.

knownPatterns.title: A panel's CACHED total reads as a live finding for a while after you fix the thing it counts
knownPatterns.detail: Measured 2026-09-17. `check-engineering-zero.mjs --project sinusoidal-cycles` reads this lane's Dependabot total from the /api/cc panel cache, not from GitHub. After a400821 closed 16 alerts, the gate still RED on exactly those 16 for ~40 minutes while `gh api repos/u00dxk2/sinusoidal-history/dependabot/alerts?state=open --paginate` — the authoritative read — already showed them gone. Read the two together before acting: the gate's own count came from a cache, so a remainder it names that matches the set you just closed is a stale total, not a second finding, and the fix is to wait for the cache rather than to waive or re-open anything. The discriminator is cheap and it is the API read, never a re-run of the gate. Same day, the same distinction held in the other direction: the 30 alerts the gate named that the API also named were real, and they took a framework bump to clear. Do not generalize this into distrust of the gate — it is right about everything it reads from the ledger, and its Dependabot leg is right as soon as the cache turns over.

knownPatterns.title: Adding a cycle updates most surfaces automatically, but two are hand-written
knownPatterns.detail: Since Phase 12, a new entry in src/data/cycles.json automatically gets its route, metadata, OG card, JSON-LD, sitemap entry, /cycles index row, and /about list row. Two surfaces do NOT update and will silently go stale: the per-cycle bullet list in public/llms.txt, and the mirror block in public/about.md. Recorded as an invariant in AGENTS.md. Also: cycle ids map to URL slugs by swapping underscores for hyphens, so renaming an id is a URL change, not a cosmetic edit.
